text: Please confirm the infant's age and describe exactly when the stridor and wheezing occur during feeding, crying, or lying down. Are there any choking episodes or coughing fits associated with these sounds?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the child ever been observed to choke or gag while breathing in (inspiratory stridor) rather than just breathing out, and do these episodes improve significantly when he is in a prone position? Also, has a head CT or swallow study been performed yet? REQUEST TEST: Upper_Airway_Swallow_Study

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia.

Based on the classic triad of inspiratory stridor worsening with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, along with the relief upon extension and occasional vomiting, the clinical picture strongly points to this congenital condition where the supraglottic tissues collapse inward during inspiration. The requested images should confirm the floppy tissue collapsing into the laryngeal inlet.
